scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of merchandising manager for THREADWORKS, an independent boutique that sells women's and men's clothing and accessories. The store owner (judge) has asked you to recommend a plan to refresh the store's window and floor displays before the fall season.

THREADWORKS has been in a downtown shopping district for nine years. Foot traffic past the store has remained steady, but fewer people are walking in. The owner believes the windows look the same as they did two years ago, and the best-selling jackets are hung in the back of the store where few customers browse. A competitor two doors down recently redesigned its windows and has seen a visible increase in shoppers.

The store's three full-time employees and two part-time workers have never received training on how to build displays. The owner's last attempt, a pile of sweaters on a table by the door, was rearranged by customers within an hour. Weekend sales account for about 55 percent of weekly revenue, and the owner knows that most shoppers decide within a few seconds whether to walk in. The store's lighting is also dim in the front third of the sales floor, and two display fixtures are damaged.

The store owner (judge) has a budget of $3,500 for the project and wants to complete it within three weeks. The recommendation should include:
- A concept for the fall window display and how it will attract passersby
- A plan for rearranging the sales floor so key products are easy to find
- How staff should greet and assist customers who enter because of the new displays
- A simple way to promote the new look and measure whether it works

You will present your recommendation to the store owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the store's office. The store owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the store owner's (judge's) questions, the store owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How would you decide which products belong in the front of the store?
What would you do if the new displays attract more visitors but do not increase sales?
How often should the displays change?
scenarios.hook: A boutique's neighbor redesigned its windows and the crowds followed.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of sales manager for SOLEMATES SHOES, a family-owned shoe store with two locations. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the store can bring more first-time customers back for a second purchase.

SOLEMATES SHOES collects names and email addresses at checkout, and about 6,000 customers are in its database. A review of the records shows that only 22 percent of customers have bought more than once. Reviews describe the staff as friendly, but customers say they are rarely contacted after a purchase and do not know about sales or new arrivals. The store has no loyalty program and does not use the database for marketing.

Customers describe the staff as pleasant but say they only hear from the store when they walk in. Returning customers spend an average of $96 per visit, compared with $61 for first-time visitors, which tells the owner that repeat business is valuable. The store runs two sales a year, and a small sign at the register invites customers to join a mailing list that has never been used. The owner is not sure whether customers want texts, email or something else.

The owner (judge) wants a plan that can start within one month and costs less than $4,000. The recommendation should include:
- How the store will use customer information to follow up after a purchase
- A loyalty approach that rewards repeat buyers without cutting profit too deeply
- How staff should ask for and use customer feedback
- How technology can support personal selling in the stores

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the owner's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Which customers should the store contact first, and why?
How would you prevent customers from feeling that the store is sending too many messages?
What would you measure after three months?
scenarios.hook: A shoe store has 6,000 customers on file and only 22 percent ever came back.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of assistant buyer for URBAN STITCH, a clothing and accessories store with a young adult customer base. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how to plan the purchase of winter merchandise after last year's winter season ended with a large amount of unsold stock.

Last winter, URBAN STITCH bought 1,200 heavy coats and sold only 700 at full price. The remaining coats were marked down by 50 percent, which cut the profit on the category nearly in half. Scarves, hats and gloves sold out in six weeks, and customers asked for them after the stock was gone. The owner has $60,000 to spend on winter merchandise this year.

Last winter's heavy coats were bought in only three sizes, and most unsold coats were in the smallest and largest sizes. The buyer who handled that season left the company, and the only records are a notebook and a spreadsheet with many blank cells. URBAN STITCH's best-selling category is denim, and its vendors require orders eight weeks before delivery, so the owner cannot change quantities late in the season. Rent and payroll are paid monthly, so unsold stock ties up cash the store needs.

The owner (judge) wants to avoid both overstocking and running out of items. The recommendation should include:
- How you will decide how much of each product category to buy
- A plan for tracking inventory during the season and acting on slow sellers
- How you would set prices and plan markdowns
- How you would work with vendors to reduce risk

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the owner's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What information from last year would you use to plan this year's purchases?
When should a markdown happen, and how large should it be?
How could a vendor help reduce the risk of overbuying?
scenarios.hook: A clothing store sold out of scarves in six weeks and discounted half its coats by 50 percent.

scenarios.judge_role: social media manager of LUXE LOOP ACCESSORIES
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of marketing coordinator for LUXE LOOP ACCESSORIES, an online retailer of handbags, jewelry and scarves. The social media manager (judge) has asked you to recommend how to use social media to launch a new line of affordable jewelry.

LUXE LOOP ACCESSORIES has 18,000 followers, but only about 2 percent engage with posts. The new jewelry line will be priced between $15 and $40 and is aimed at college students and young professionals. The company has $5,000 to spend on promotion for the launch and has never worked with an influencer before.

LUXE LOOP ACCESSORIES ships from a small warehouse and offers free returns within 30 days. Its handbags are well known among customers in their thirties, but the company has had little success with younger shoppers. The jewelry line was designed by two recent design school graduates who also manage the company's photography. A competitor recently ran a giveaway with a well-known college creator and added 4,000 followers in a week, and the owner has asked whether LUXE LOOP should do the same.

The social media manager (judge) wants a plan that reaches the right audience and stays within budget. The recommendation should include:
- How the brand should be presented in the launch posts
- Which social media platforms to focus on and why
- Whether to work with influencers and how to choose them
- How the budget will be divided and how the results will be measured

You will present your recommendation to the social media manager (judge) in a role-play to take place in the company's office. The social media manager (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the social media manager's (judge's) questions, the social media manager (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What would make an influencer a good fit for the brand?
How would you decide whether to spend more on a platform that is working?
What could go wrong if an influencer posts something that does not match the brand?
scenarios.hook: An accessories brand has 18,000 followers, a $5,000 launch budget and almost no engagement.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of marketing manager for NORTHSTAR DENIM, a regional jeans company sold in 40 department stores and through its own website. The vice president of marketing (judge) has asked you to recommend how to reach a new segment of customers who want sustainable clothing, without losing the company's current buyers.

NORTHSTAR DENIM's current customers are mostly adults aged 30 to 50 who value fit and durability. Sales have been flat for two years, while two newer brands that use recycled cotton and publish their factory conditions have grown 25 percent. Customer interviews show that younger shoppers think NORTHSTAR is "my parents' brand." Producing a line using recycled materials would raise the cost per pair by about $9 and require retail prices of $98 to $120.

The company's two newer competitors both donate a share of profit to environmental groups, and one prints the country and factory of each garment on its tags. NORTHSTAR DENIM manufactures in the United States and Mexico and has a reputation for jeans that last ten years or more, but it has never promoted this publicly. About 60 percent of its sales come through department stores, which expect the company to keep prices stable and to support new lines with advertising.

The vice president (judge) wants to decide within a month whether to launch the new line. The recommendation should include:
- How the new segment should be described and why it is attractive
- How the new line should be positioned against the two growing competitors
- How the new line can be marketed without alienating current customers
- Which risks the company should consider before launching

You will present your recommendation to the vice president of marketing (judge) in a role-play to take place in the vice president's office. The vice president of marketing (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the vice president's (judge's) questions, the vice president of marketing (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How would you test interest in the new line before committing to a full launch?
What message would you avoid using because it might hurt the current brand?
How should the company price the new line compared with its existing jeans?
scenarios.hook: A denim brand is called "my parents' brand" while two eco-minded rivals grow 25 percent.

scenarios.judge_role: owner of BELLE & BEAU BRIDAL ACCESSORIES
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of sales manager for BELLE & BEAU BRIDAL ACCESSORIES, a store that sells veils, jewelry, hair pieces and wedding party gifts. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how to increase the average sale, which has been stagnant at $140, without discouraging brides who are watching their budgets.

Most brides visit the store once, about six months before their wedding, and many leave after buying only one item. A review of sales shows that bridesmaid gifts and groomsmen items are almost never purchased with the bride's items, though the store carries them. Competing online stores offer a bundle discount, and customers have asked why the store does not.

The store occupies 1,600 square feet in a shopping center and employs four people, including two part-time college students. Brides usually come in with their mothers or a close friend, and staff say that the mother often decides the budget while the bride makes the style choice. Wedding season runs from April through October, and the store's slow months are January and February, when sales fall by nearly two-thirds. The owner has also noticed that many brides ask for matching items for the groom's party that the store does not stock.

The owner (judge) wants a plan that raises the average sale by at least 15 percent in four months. The recommendation should include:
- How the product mix should be organized to suggest complete purchases
- How staff should use suggestive selling and cross-selling without being pushy
- A pricing approach that includes bundles and protects profit
- How buying behavior of brides and their families should influence the plan

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the store's back office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Who else besides the bride influences what is purchased, and how should staff involve them?
How would you set a bundle price so that the store does not lose money?
When is a suggestion to add another item likely to feel pushy?
scenarios.hook: A bridal accessories store's average sale is stuck at $140 and bridesmaid gifts rarely sell.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of operations manager for THE VINTAGE RACK, a secondhand clothing store that buys items from the public and resells them in-store and on a growing website. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend a system for managing inventory now that online sales have grown from 10 to 40 percent of revenue.

THE VINTAGE RACK carries about 3,500 one-of-a-kind items, which means each item can only be sold once. Staff track online items on a spreadsheet and in-store items by tags, and in the past month 31 items were sold twice, one online and one in the store. Customers who were told an item was gone have left negative reviews. Staff also report spending about 12 hours a week photographing and listing items.

Staff photograph each item with a phone and list it themselves, which means listing quality varies, and several customers have complained that the condition of items looked better online than in person. THE VINTAGE RACK pays sellers either cash or store credit, and about half of sellers choose credit, which brings them back to shop. The owner has considered adding a second employee dedicated to online orders and pays $2,400 a month in rent for the store.

The owner (judge) wants to fix the problem within two months and has up to $8,000 to spend. The recommendation should include:
- How to track one-of-a-kind items accurately across the store and the website
- What technology to adopt and how staff will be trained to use it
- How to handle customers when an item is sold twice
- How the purchasing process should change as online sales grow

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the store's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What should staff say to a customer whose purchased item is no longer available?
How would you decide which items are worth the time to photograph and list online?
What would you do first if the new system is more expensive than $8,000?
scenarios.hook: A vintage clothing store sold 31 one-of-a-kind items twice in a single month.

scenarios.judge_role: chief merchandising officer of ATLAS ATHLETIC
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of senior marketing manager for ATLAS ATHLETIC, a national company that sells running shoes and athletic apparel through 85 stores and online. The chief merchandising officer (judge) has asked you to recommend a marketing plan for a new line of women's trail running shoes.

Women account for 38 percent of ATLAS ATHLETIC's footwear sales, but fewer than 10 percent of its trail shoe sales. Research shows that women who run trails often find that men's shoes fit poorly and that stores carry few options. Three competitors have recently launched women's-specific trail lines, and one has sponsored popular female athletes and a trail running series. The product launch budget is $2.4 million for the first year.

ATLAS ATHLETIC's trail line currently uses the same sizing patterns across men's and women's shoes, and customer reviews on its website say that women's sizes run wide in the heel. The company's stores in mountain regions report the highest trail sales, while stores in large cities report very few. The company has relationships with 14 running clubs, only two of which focus on trail running or have a majority of women as members. The board will meet in a month to approve or reject next year's budgets.

The chief merchandising officer (judge) wants a plan that the board can approve next month. The recommendation should include:
- How the target market should be described and what additional research is needed
- How the new line should be positioned within the ATLAS ATHLETIC brand
- A promotional plan that divides the budget across in-store, online and event activities
- How success will be measured in the first 12 months

You will present your recommendation to the chief merchandising officer (judge) in a role-play to take place in the executive conference room. The chief merchandising officer (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the chief merchandising officer's (judge's) questions, the chief merchandising officer (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What research would you do before spending the full launch budget?
How could the company avoid being seen as simply making a smaller version of a men's shoe?
What results after six months would make you change the plan?
scenarios.hook: A running brand sells women 38 percent of its shoes but fewer than 10 percent of its trail shoes.

scenarios.judge_role: director of e-commerce for CEDAR & CO. MENSWEAR
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of e-commerce manager for CEDAR & CO. MENSWEAR, a retailer of suits, dress shirts and accessories with 12 stores and an online shop. The director of e-commerce (judge) has asked you to recommend how to reduce the high rate of returns that is cutting into online profit.

About 34 percent of online orders are returned, compared with 12 percent in stores. Most returns are for sizing and fit. Each return costs the company about $11 in shipping and handling, and returned dress shirts often cannot be sold at full price. The company offers free shipping and free returns, and a competitor has just announced a size-matching tool. Online sales are $14 million a year.

Customer service reports show that the three most common reasons for return are that the shirt was too tight in the neck, that the jacket sleeves were too long and that the color looked different from the photograph. The online store uses one size chart for all products, though the company sells three different fits. The warehouse team says that returned items sit for about nine days before being restocked, during which time they are not available for sale, and the company has no way to see which customers return the most.

The director (judge) wants a plan that cuts the return rate to below 25 percent without reducing sales. The recommendation should include:
- How the company can use customer feedback and data to find the causes of returns
- Technology that can help customers choose the right size
- Whether to change the return and shipping policy and how that would affect pricing
- How the changes will be communicated to customers

You will present your recommendation to the director of e-commerce (judge) in a role-play to take place in the director's office. The director of e-commerce (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the director's (judge's) questions, the director of e-commerce (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What risks come with charging customers for returns?
How would you use the store locations to help reduce online returns?
What information would you collect from customers who return an item?
scenarios.hook: Over a third of one retailer's online orders come back, and each costs $11 to process.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of brand manager for KINDRED KNITS, a company that sells sweaters, scarves and blankets and promotes itself as "ethically made." The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how to respond after a news story reported poor working conditions at one of the company's overseas suppliers.

The supplier makes about 30 percent of KINDRED KNITS products. The story included photographs of crowded rooms and workers who said they were required to work overtime without pay. The company's own audit last year rated the supplier "acceptable," and the owner did not review the full report. Social media posts about the story have been shared 9,000 times, and two retail partners have asked for a response within a week.

KINDRED KNITS was founded eight years ago by two siblings who describe the company's values on every label and package. About 70 percent of its customers say in surveys that ethical sourcing is an important reason they buy. The company's largest retail partner has said it will review its agreement if the issue is not handled openly. A nonprofit that monitors workplace conditions has offered to inspect the factory, but the inspection would cost $12,000 and could reveal more problems.

The owner (judge) wants to protect both the workers and the brand. The recommendation should include:
- What the company should say publicly in the next 48 hours
- How the company should work with the supplier and whether to keep it
- How the company will make sure its marketing claims about ethical production are accurate
- A plan to rebuild customer trust over the next six months

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the owner's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What would you do if the supplier denies the allegations?
Should the company change its "ethically made" claim for now? Why or why not?
How would you measure whether customer trust is returning?
scenarios.hook: A sweater brand that markets itself as "ethically made" faces a news story about its supplier.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of service advisor for QUICKLANE AUTO CARE, an independent repair shop with six bays that handles oil changes, brakes, tires and general repairs. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the shop's service advisors should talk with customers at the front counter.

QUICKLANE AUTO CARE has been open for 11 years and relies on repeat business. Online reviews describe the mechanics as skilled, but many customers say that the front counter feels rushed, that they were not told what repairs would cost before work began and that no one followed up after their visit. Last quarter, 18 customers who had come in for an oil change left without agreeing to recommended brake work, and three later complained that the shop never explained why the repair mattered.

The shop's advisors are paid a small bonus for each additional repair they sell, and the owner worries that this has caused some advisors to push customers instead of listening. The shop completes about 60 vehicles a week, and a typical repair ticket is $310.

The owner (judge) wants a plan that improves customer satisfaction without lowering the shop's income. The recommendation should include:
- How advisors should greet customers and uncover what each customer needs and can afford
- How to explain a recommended repair so customers understand the reason and the cost
- How the shop should follow up after the repair is complete
- How to change the bonus plan so that service comes first

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the shop's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What should an advisor say to a customer who declines a recommended repair?
How would you describe the difference between a needed repair and a repair that could wait?
What would you measure to find out whether customers are more satisfied?
scenarios.hook: A repair shop's mechanics are praised, yet customers leave the front counter feeling rushed.

scenarios.judge_role: service manager of HARBORVIEW TIRE & WARRANTY
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of assistant service manager for HARBORVIEW TIRE & WARRANTY, a tire and brake center with three locations. The service manager (judge) has asked you to explain how the company should handle warranties and guarantees on its products and to recommend how staff should describe them to customers.

HARBORVIEW TIRE & WARRANTY sells four grades of tires, ranging from a $89 economy tire to a $240 premium tire. The premium tires include a 60,000-mile treadwear guarantee, while the economy tires carry only a 12-month defect warranty. Last month, a customer returned with tires that had worn out at 30,000 miles and said a salesperson had promised the tires would last "for years." The company could not find the promise in writing, and the customer filed a complaint with a consumer protection agency.

Staff are also unsure how to explain the difference between a warranty from the manufacturer and a guarantee from the shop. About 14 percent of customers request some kind of warranty claim in the first year, and each claim that is handled poorly can cost the company a customer who spends about $700 a year.

The service manager (judge) wants clear and honest practices that comply with the law. The recommendation should include:
- How staff should explain the grades of tires and what each warranty or guarantee covers
- What should be put in writing and given to customers at the time of sale
- What customers' rights are under consumer protection rules, and how the company should respond to a complaint
- How to train staff so that they never promise more than the company can deliver

You will present your recommendation to the service manager (judge) in a role-play to take place in the manager's office. The service manager (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the service manager's (judge's) questions, the service manager (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How should the company handle the customer whose tires wore out at 30,000 miles?
Why is it risky for a salesperson to describe how long a product will last?
What should staff do if a manufacturer's warranty and the shop's guarantee conflict?
scenarios.hook: A customer says a salesperson promised tires would last for years, and nothing was in writing.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of marketing coordinator for ROADSTAR DETAILING, a car wash and detailing business with two locations in a suburban area. The marketing manager (judge) has asked you to recommend how to promote a new monthly membership plan that offers unlimited washes for $29.

ROADSTAR DETAILING has about 2,200 regular customers and serves roughly 400 cars on a typical weekend. Most customers pay $12 to $18 for a single wash, and the company believes that a membership would raise the number of visits and give more predictable income. The membership program launches in six weeks, and the company's goal is to sign up 500 members within three months.

The company has never done much advertising. It has a small sign at the entrance, a website with limited information and a page on social media with 900 followers. A rival car wash across town advertises heavily on local radio and with coupons in the mail, and its prices are lower. The promotion budget is $4,500.

The marketing manager (judge) wants a plan that fits within the budget and reaches current and new customers. The recommendation should include:
- A description of the role promotion plays in launching the membership and which types of promotion to use
- How to combine at least three elements of the promotional mix
- Which advertising media to use and why
- How to encourage word of mouth among existing customers

You will present your recommendation to the marketing manager (judge) in a role-play to take place in the company's office. The marketing manager (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the marketing manager's (judge's) questions, the marketing manager (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How would you promote the membership to customers who already visit often?
Which of your promotions would you cut first if the budget were reduced?
How could the company find out which promotion brought in the most new members?
scenarios.hook: A car wash wants 500 members in three months with $4,500 and a rival that advertises on the radio.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of store manager for TOPGEAR PARTS & ACCESSORIES, a retail store that sells car batteries, wiper blades, floor mats and other automotive items to drivers and small repair shops. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the store should set prices after a competitor began advertising lower prices on batteries.

TOPGEAR PARTS & ACCESSORIES sells a standard car battery for $149, which includes a 3-year free replacement warranty. The nearest competitor, an online seller, lists a similar battery for $119 but charges $15 for shipping and offers a 1-year warranty. Battery sales have dropped 22 percent in two months, though sales of wiper blades and floor mats have held steady. The store pays about $96 for each battery and has high fixed costs, including rent and a staff of seven.

The owner is considering a price cut to $125 on batteries, which would reduce profit on each sale from $53 to $29. The store also sets its prices by hand, and a recent audit found that 40 items were priced differently on the shelf than at the register, which could lead to complaints.

The owner (judge) wants a pricing approach that is competitive, legal and fair. The recommendation should include:
- The factors that should influence the price of the battery
- Whether to match the competitor and how to defend the value of the store's warranty
- How the store should handle pricing mistakes and make sure advertised prices are honest
- How technology can help the store keep prices accurate

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the owner's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How would you explain to a customer why your battery costs more than the online price?
What legal problems could come from advertising a battery price that is not available at the register?
Under what conditions would you agree to lower the price?
scenarios.hook: A parts store's battery sales fell 22 percent after an online rival undercut it by $30.

scenarios.judge_role: director of marketing at ROADWISE FLEET SERVICES
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of marketing research analyst for ROADWISE FLEET SERVICES, a company that maintains vehicles for small businesses such as delivery companies, plumbers and landscapers. The director of marketing (judge) has asked you to design a research study to find out why customers leave the company after their first year.

ROADWISE FLEET SERVICES has 640 customers and loses about 30 percent of them within 12 months. Exit interviews have been informal, and the sales team believes customers leave because of price. However, several former customers have mentioned that repair times were longer than promised, and one said that the company's invoices were confusing. The company has customer records that include contract size, type of vehicle and repair history, but no survey has ever been conducted.

The company has $10,000 to spend on research and wants results within six weeks, before the next budget cycle. About 70 percent of customers are small businesses with fewer than five vehicles, and the owners are often busy and difficult to reach.

The director of marketing (judge) wants research that leads to clear action. The recommendation should include:
- A statement of the research problem and how the research will answer it
- The options the company has for obtaining information, including data it already has
- How data should be collected from busy business owners, including how the questionnaire should be designed
- How to avoid mistakes that could make the results misleading

You will present your recommendation to the director of marketing (judge) in a role-play to take place in the director's office. The director of marketing (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the director's (judge's) questions, the director of marketing (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What would you do with the company's existing records before collecting any new data?
How would you avoid asking leading questions in the survey?
What would you tell the sales team if the research shows price is not the main reason customers leave?
scenarios.hook: A fleet repair company loses 30 percent of its customers a year and blames price without proof.

scenarios.judge_role: owner of PIT STOP QUICK LUBE
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of customer relations manager for PIT STOP QUICK LUBE, a chain of five oil change and maintenance shops. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how to build lasting relationships with customers and turn first-time visitors into repeat customers.

PIT STOP QUICK LUBE serves about 1,100 vehicles a week across its five shops. A review of customer records shows that only 38 percent of customers come back within a year, though the company's own advice is that most vehicles need service every six months. The shops collect each customer's name, phone number and vehicle details but do not use them for marketing. Customers have said that the shops are fast but impersonal, and that they often forget when their next service is due.

The company has a small budget of $7,000 for a program that could begin in two months. One shop manager has suggested a punch-card program, while another has said that text reminders would work better. The owner is also worried about contacting customers too often or sharing their information improperly.

The owner (judge) wants a program that increases repeat visits in a way that respects customers. The recommendation should include:
- How the company will build a clientele and what factors build loyalty in this business
- What a customer relationship management system should track and how it should be used
- How and when to follow up with customers after each visit
- How the company will use technology while protecting customer privacy and trust

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the owner's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Which is more effective for this business: a punch card, a text reminder or something else, and why?
How often should the company contact a customer before it becomes annoying?
What information should the company never collect or share?
scenarios.hook: Only 38 percent of one chain's oil change customers return within a year.

scenarios.judge_role: marketing director of AUTOLINK DIGITAL MOTORS
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of digital marketing manager for AUTOLINK DIGITAL MOTORS, a used-car dealership group with four lots and an online showroom. The marketing director (judge) has asked you to recommend how to use digital marketing to bring more qualified buyers to the dealerships.

AUTOLINK DIGITAL MOTORS sells about 260 vehicles a month and spends $38,000 a month on marketing, of which 60 percent goes to listing sites and print. The company's website receives 24,000 visits a month, but only 1.2 percent of visitors request a test drive. Analytics show that most visitors leave after viewing a single vehicle page, and that mobile users, who make up 68 percent of traffic, leave even faster. Competitors have begun using short videos and local social media ads.

The marketing director must decide within a month how to rebalance the budget. The company's website was built five years ago and is slow to load, and none of the four lots keeps its inventory photographs consistent.

The marketing director (judge) wants a digital plan that improves results without raising the total budget. The recommendation should include:
- How technology has changed the way customers shop for vehicles and how that affects promotion
- Which online advertising and email tactics to prioritize
- How to use social media for digital marketing and how to get found through search
- How the company will track results and decide where to shift spending

You will present your recommendation to the marketing director (judge) in a role-play to take place in the director's office. The marketing director (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the marketing director's (judge's) questions, the marketing director (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What would you fix on the website first to improve mobile visitors' experience?
How would you decide which part of the print and listing budget to move?
What measures would show whether the digital changes are working?
scenarios.hook: A dealership's website gets 24,000 visits a month and only 1.2 percent ask for a test drive.

scenarios.judge_role: chief marketing officer of MERIDIAN AUTO GROUP
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of marketing planning manager for MERIDIAN AUTO GROUP, a regional chain of 12 dealerships and service centers selling new and used vehicles. The chief marketing officer (judge) has asked you to develop the marketing plan for the group's service centers for the coming year.

The service centers earn 46 percent of the group's profit but have received only 15 percent of the marketing budget. Service revenue has been flat for three years, even though the number of vehicles sold has risen. Independent shops and quick-lube chains have taken customers with lower prices, and many customers do not realize that they can get the same service from the dealership at competitive rates. The company's board wants service revenue to grow by 9 percent next year, and the proposed budget for service marketing is $850,000.

The group's customer data shows that 55 percent of people who buy a vehicle never return for service. Vehicle sales are expected to fall by about 6 percent next year because of higher interest rates.

The chief marketing officer (judge) wants a plan the board can approve. The recommendation should include:
- A situation analysis of the service business, including strengths, weaknesses, competitors and trends
- How the plan connects to a forecast of the service business and the 9 percent goal
- A promotional plan that divides the budget across activities and a timeline
- How the company will measure results and adjust the plan during the year

You will present your recommendation to the chief marketing officer (judge) in a role-play to take place in the executive conference room. The chief marketing officer (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the chief marketing officer's (judge's) questions, the chief marketing officer (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How would your forecast change if vehicle sales fall more than expected?
Which part of the plan would you protect first if the budget were cut by 20 percent?
Why do so many vehicle buyers never return for service, and how would you address it?
scenarios.hook: A dealership group's service centers make 46 percent of its profit and get 15 percent of its marketing.

scenarios.judge_role: vice president of EXPRESSWAY PARTS DISTRIBUTION
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of channel manager for EXPRESSWAY PARTS DISTRIBUTION, a company that supplies replacement auto parts to 1,800 independent repair shops and to a growing online store. The vice president (judge) has asked you to recommend how to manage relationships with the company's distribution partners after a conflict over online sales.

EXPRESSWAY PARTS DISTRIBUTION launched an online store two years ago that sells directly to drivers at prices lower than those charged by the repair shops. Several large repair shops have complained that this undercuts their business, and four have threatened to switch to a competing supplier. Together those four shops account for $5.2 million in annual sales. At the same time, the online store has grown by 40 percent and has brought in customers who were not previously served.

The company has also been approached by a national retailer that wants to carry EXPRESSWAY's most popular parts under its own name, which would create a new partnership but could further upset the repair shops.

The vice president (judge) wants to keep the company's channel partners while continuing to grow. The recommendation should include:
- How to coordinate the online store and the repair shop channel with other marketing activities
- How the company should describe its relationship with channel members and affinity partners, and what it owes each
- What legal and ethical considerations affect pricing and exclusivity in the channel
- Whether to accept the retailer's offer and how to communicate the decision

You will present your recommendation to the vice president (judge) in a role-play to take place in the executive office. The vice president (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the vice president's (judge's) questions, the vice president (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How could the company keep the repair shops loyal without limiting the online store?
What are the risks of letting the national retailer sell under its own name?
What would you tell the four shops that are thinking of leaving?
scenarios.hook: Four repair shops worth $5.2 million threaten to leave over a parts distributor's online store.

scenarios.judge_role: director of customer insights at VELOCITY MOTORS
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of senior marketing analyst for VELOCITY MOTORS, a car manufacturer's regional sales office that supports 40 dealerships. The director of customer insights (judge) has asked you to recommend how to use customer data to personalize marketing while protecting customer privacy.

VELOCITY MOTORS has data from 310,000 customers, including purchase history, service visits, website activity and responses to past campaigns. Its current campaigns send the same message to everyone, and only 0.8 percent of customers respond. A pilot at three dealerships that used purchase and service history to recommend upgrades or trade-ins doubled the response rate to 1.7 percent. However, a customer recently complained that a message mentioned a repair that she thought was private, and a data security audit found that customer records are stored in six different systems.

The company has a budget of $620,000 for the next phase. State regulations on the use of customer data are changing, and the company plans to begin using real-time offers on its website.

The director of customer insights (judge) wants a plan that improves results and protects customers. The recommendation should include:
- How customer data should be used to recommend personalized, relevant campaigns
- How the company could customize website and in-store interactions in real time
- How analytics tools will be used to track behavior and results
- How marketing data should be secured, stored and protected from misuse

You will present your recommendation to the director of customer insights (judge) in a role-play to take place in the director's office. The director of customer insights (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the director's (judge's) questions, the director of customer insights (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What personalization would you avoid because customers may find it intrusive?
How would you handle the data stored in six different systems?
How would you measure whether personalization is worth its cost?
scenarios.hook: Personalized messages doubled one carmaker's response rate and then upset a customer.

scenarios.judge_role: human resources manager of BIG CITY TRANSIT
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an employee in the human resources department at LAKESHORE TRANSIT, a city bus system with 240 drivers and 40 office staff. The human resources manager (judge) wants you to explain how the department helps new drivers get started and what rights they have.

LAKESHORE TRANSIT hired 35 new drivers this spring. Several of them said they did not know whom to report problems to, and two did not know that they were entitled to rest breaks. One new driver went straight to the general manager with a schedule complaint instead of speaking with a supervisor first.

The human resources manager (judge) asks you to explain what human resources management does, what an orientation for new drivers should include, why the chain of command matters and which rights workers have.

followup_questions: Who should a new driver speak with first about a schedule problem?
Why is it important for workers to know their rights from the first day?
scenarios.hook: Thirty-five new bus drivers started this spring and many did not know who to ask for help.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an assistant at ACE ELECTRIC, an electrical contracting company with eight employees. The owner (judge) wants you to explain the different ways a business can be owned and why following laws and company rules matters as the company grows.

The company began as a one-person business and is owned entirely by the owner. The owner is thinking about adding a partner who would invest $60,000 and help manage the crews. Last month, an inspector found that a job had been started without a required permit. The owner says that permits take too long and slow down projects.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain the main types of business ownership, why management and following company policies are important and why the company should comply with the intent of regulations and not only their wording.

followup_questions: What is one advantage and one disadvantage of taking on a partner?
What could happen to the company if it keeps skipping permits?
scenarios.hook: An electrician weighs taking a partner after an inspector finds a job started without a permit.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a sales associate at TECH TOWN, an electronics store with 25 employees. The store manager (judge) wants you to explain how employees can manage their time better during the busy holiday season.

TECH TOWN employees have been asked to stock shelves, help customers, process online orders and attend training sessions. Last year, shelves were not restocked on time, two online orders shipped late and several employees reported feeling overwhelmed. The store manager has noticed that employees who plan their tasks each day miss fewer deadlines.

followup_questions: How should an employee decide which task to do first?
What should an employee do if they cannot meet a deadline?
scenarios.hook: An electronics store's holiday rush left shelves empty and two online orders late.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a teacher's assistant at LITTLE LEAF DAYCARE, a center that cares for 70 children. The owner (judge) wants you to explain why information about children and families must be kept private.

LITTLE LEAF DAYCARE keeps records of each child's allergies, medical conditions, pickup contacts and family situations. Last week, a staff member mentioned a family's financial trouble to a parent from another family while chatting at pickup. followup_questions: What should staff do with printed records when they are not in use?
How should an employee respond when a parent asks about another family?
scenarios.hook: A daycare worker's chat at pickup exposed one family's private troubles to another.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a safety coordinator at RIDGELINE FOODS, a packaged-food plant with 180 employees on two shifts. The plant manager (judge) wants you to explain the plant's safety responsibilities after a state inspector's visit.

The inspector cited the plant for blocked exits near the packing line and a missing emergency eyewash station. An employee also told you that a coworker has been bypassing a machine guard to work faster, and no one has reported it. Last year, the plant recorded 9 injuries, and the plant manager wants that number cut in half.

followup_questions: What should you do about the employee bypassing the machine guard?
How should the plant make sure that employees feel safe reporting problems?
scenarios.hook: A food plant with nine injuries last year fails an inspection for blocked exits.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a lead trainer at HILLTOP FITNESS, a gym with 14 trainers. The manager (judge) wants you to explain how to lead and coach a team that has lost its energy since the gym's busiest instructor left.

Since the departure, group class attendance has fallen 20 percent. Trainers are working in separate groups, and a few have said that leaders at the gym do not listen. Two new trainers say they do not feel ready to lead classes, and one gave unclear directions that left a class confused about a piece of equipment.

The manager (judge) asks you to explain what leadership means in this setting, how you would coach the new trainers and how trainers can work well as a team and give clear directions to members.

followup_questions: What would a coaching conversation with a new trainer include?
How can a leader show that they are listening to the team?

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an operations assistant at PAPER TRAIL BOOKS, an independent bookstore that also sells coffee and hosts community events. The owner (judge) has been asked to explain at a chamber of commerce meeting what value a business creates for its customers.

The store sells new and used books, offers a reading space with seating and holds weekly events for children and adults. A customer survey showed that many shoppers value the store's location, its recommendations and its late weekend hours, even though most books cost $2 to $4 more than online. The store uses about 1,800 square feet of rented space and employs eight people.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain what economics is, what resources the store uses and what types of economic utility the store provides.

You will present your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the bookstore. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the meeting. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How does being open late on weekends create value for customers?
What resources would the store lose if it moved online only?
scenarios.hook: A bookstore charges $2 to $4 more than online and customers keep coming anyway.

scenarios.judge_role: chief operating officer of SUMMIT CONTRACTORS
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a project coordinator at SUMMIT CONTRACTORS, a construction company with 90 employees. The chief operating officer (judge) wants you to explain how to manage a 14-week renovation of a library that has fallen two weeks behind schedule.

The project has a $1.8 million budget and involves the electrical, plumbing and painting teams. A delay in delivery of windows has pushed back the painting crew, and the electrical team has reported that two required inspections are not yet scheduled. The library has told the company that it must reopen by the date in the contract, or the company will pay a penalty of $2,500 a day.

The chief operating officer (judge) asks you to explain how the project should have been planned, how you would monitor and correct the delays and how you would decide whether the project was a success.

You will present your recommendation to the chief operating officer (judge) in a role-play to take place at the company's headquarters. The chief operating officer (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the project. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the chief operating officer's (judge's) questions, the chief operating officer (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What would you change first to get the project back on schedule?
Besides finishing on time, how would you measure whether the project succeeded?
scenarios.hook: A $1.8 million library renovation is two weeks late with $2,500 a day in penalties looming.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an assistant manager at CORNER BAKE SHOP, a bakery that has used the same menu and the same morning schedule for 15 years. The owner (judge) wants your help leading a change after a drop in sales.

Sales have declined 14 percent in two years, and customers say the shop is out of popular items by 10:00 a.m. Most baking happens between 3:00 and 7:00 a.m., and the owner is reluctant to alter either the menu or the schedule. Three longtime bakers have said they do not want to change how things have always been done. A younger employee has suggested adding an afternoon bake and an online preorder system.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain how to make a good decision here, how to solve the problem and how to lead the change while keeping the team on board.

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the bakery's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the sales. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How would you respond to the bakers who do not want to change?
What would you test first before making the whole change?
scenarios.hook: A bakery that has run the same way for 15 years lost 14 percent of its sales.

scenarios.judge_role: director of GRANITE STATE CREDIT SERVICES
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a business analyst at GRANITE STATE CREDIT SERVICES, a company that processes payments for 300 local merchants. The director (judge) wants your advice on how to use the company's data to decide where to expand.

The company has five years of transaction data that show higher growth in two counties. A consulting firm's report, paid for by a software vendor, recommends a costly new analytics system. A trade association survey of 40 merchants says most want faster payment processing, but the survey was sent only to the association's members. The director must present a plan to the board in a month.

The director (judge) asks you to explain how to judge the quality and sources of the information available, what data mining could show and how technology might change the way the company works.

You will present your recommendation to the director (judge) in a role-play to take place at the company's office. The director (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the data. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the director's (judge's) questions, the director (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Why might the consulting firm's report be less reliable than the transaction data?
What conclusion would you avoid drawing from the merchant survey?
scenarios.hook: A payments company has five years of data, a vendor-funded report and a survey of 40 merchants.

scenarios.judge_role: owner of GREEN THUMB GARDEN SHOP
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a part-time employee at GREEN THUMB GARDEN SHOP, a small business that sells plants, soil and gardening tools. The owner (judge) wants you to explain what makes a small business important to the local economy.

GREEN THUMB GARDEN SHOP is owned by one person and employs six people, mostly students. The owner buys many plants from nearby growers and pays about $18,000 a year in local taxes. A home improvement chain recently began selling plants and tools at lower prices, and the owner is worried about whether the shop can stay profitable.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain the types of activities a business carries out, how a small business like this helps the local economy and what affects the shop's profit.

You will explain your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the shop. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the shop's role in town. followup_questions: What does the shop provide to the community besides products?
What is one way the shop could protect its profit against the chain?
scenarios.hook: A garden shop that pays $18,000 in local taxes is undercut by a home improvement chain.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a high school junior who helps at SPARK TUTORING, a small business that matches students with tutors. The founder (judge) wants you to explain what it takes to be an entrepreneur after a classmate asked about starting a business.

SPARK TUTORING began two years ago with the founder as the only tutor and now has 11 tutors and 90 regular students. The founder works about 55 hours a week and has said that the business has been rewarding and stressful. Your classmate wants to open a similar business but has never managed money or people.

The founder (judge) asks you to explain what career opportunities exist in entrepreneurship, what strengths and weaknesses a new entrepreneur should assess and why confidence and responsibility are important.

You will explain your ideas to the founder (judge) in a role-play to take place in the company's office. The founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about your classmate. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the founder's (judge's) questions, the founder (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What is one weakness your classmate could work on before starting a business?
Why does an owner need to take responsibility for mistakes?
scenarios.hook: A tutoring founder works 55 hours a week while a classmate asks how to start a business.

scenarios.judge_role: owner of ROLLING PINS FOOD TRUCK
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a cashier at ROLLING PINS FOOD TRUCK, a truck that sells pastries and sandwiches near an office park and a college. The owner (judge) wants you to explain how to set prices and manage risk as a new competitor arrives.

ROLLING PINS sells a pastry for $4. The price of butter has risen 25 percent, and another truck, which sells a similar pastry for $3.50, has begun parking nearby on the days the college is in session. On rainy days, sales drop by about half. The owner has a $9,000 loan on the truck and cannot afford a losing month.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain how supply and demand and competition affect the price of a pastry and what risks the truck faces.

You will explain your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the truck. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about prices. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What could the truck do on rainy days to reduce its losses?
Should the truck lower its price to match the other truck? Why or why not?
scenarios.hook: A pastry truck faces 25 percent costlier butter and a $3.50 rival, with a $9,000 loan to repay.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an assistant at PEBBLE & PINE, a startup that sells handmade wooden toys online. The co-founder (judge) wants you to explain how an owner should handle money in the first year of a business.

The company earned $42,000 in its first year, and the two co-founders each took out $1,500 a month for personal expenses. At the end of the year, they were unsure how much was profit and how much was needed for new tools and materials. One co-founder suggested using business money to pay a personal credit card bill.

The co-founder (judge) asks you to explain how an owner earns income, how to budget between business and personal needs and why keeping financial records matters.

You will explain your ideas to the co-founder (judge) in a role-play to take place in the workshop. The co-founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the finances. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the co-founder's (judge's) questions, the co-founder (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Why should the business and the owners keep separate accounts?
How should the owners decide how much of the money to take out each month?
scenarios.hook: Two toy makers earned $42,000 in a year and cannot tell how much of it was profit.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a customer support associate at FIELD & FORK MEALS, a start-up that delivers weekly meal kits made with ingredients from local farms. The founder (judge) wants you to explain how employees can show initiative to help a young company grow.

FIELD & FORK MEALS has 14 employees and 1,100 weekly subscribers. About 1 in 5 new customers cancels within a month, and the common reasons are that boxes arrive late and recipes are too complicated. The founder says that most employees wait to be told what to do, and the company's way of doing things has not changed since it began.

The founder (judge) asks you to explain what initiative looks like in a start-up, why employees should sometimes challenge how things are done and how to make decisions and solve the cancellation problem.

You will present your ideas to the founder (judge) in a role-play to take place in the company's office. The founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the cancellations. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the founder's (judge's) questions, the founder (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What is one thing an employee could do on their own to reduce cancellations?
How should the company decide which idea from employees to try first?
scenarios.hook: A meal-kit startup loses one in five new customers within a month.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a business student working part-time at HOLLOW OAK CANDLES, a company that makes and sells soy candles at markets and online. The owner (judge) wants you to explain what financial information shows about whether the business is doing well.

HOLLOW OAK CANDLES sold $85,000 of candles last year, which felt like a success. The owner paid $31,000 for wax, jars and scents, $12,000 for market fees and shipping and $9,000 for equipment. The owner took home only $14,000 and does not understand why so little remained.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain what accounting tells a business owner, what factors affect profit and why financial information matters for decisions like pricing and spending.

You will present your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the workshop. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the profit. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Which cost would you look at first to find savings?
What financial information should the owner review each month?
scenarios.hook: A candle maker sold $85,000 in a year and took home $14,000.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an operations assistant at CLEARVIEW WINDOW WASH, a business that cleans windows for stores and office buildings. The owner (judge) wants your advice on legal protection after an employee fell from a ladder at a customer's building.

CLEARVIEW WINDOW WASH is a sole proprietorship with four employees. The employee was not seriously hurt, but the building owner has said the company could be responsible for damage to a glass door. The owner does not have written safety procedures and carries only a basic insurance policy. A partner has suggested changing the business to a corporation.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain how the type of ownership affects the owner's risk, what insurance does and why the company should follow safety laws.
