After you have presented your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What risk does the owner face personally as a sole proprietor?
What written procedure would you create first?
scenarios.hook: A window washer's employee fell from a ladder and the owner's personal assets could be at stake.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a product assistant at ECHO LEARNING, a start-up that makes a language-learning app used by 25,000 people. The founder (judge) wants your advice on whether to build a new feature that uses voice recognition to give pronunciation feedback.

The feature would cost about $120,000 to develop and take six months. Surveys show that 60 percent of users want help with speaking, but the app's main competitor has just announced a similar feature. The start-up has about eight months of cash left and a small team of nine.

The founder (judge) asks you to explain why innovation skills matter, what value the new feature would create for users and the economy, and what risks the company takes by building it.

You will present your recommendation to the founder (judge) in a role-play to take place in the company's office. The founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the feature. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the founder's (judge's) questions, the founder (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What is the biggest risk in spending $120,000 on this feature?
How could the company test the idea at a lower cost first?
scenarios.hook: A language app weighs a $120,000 feature while its competitor announces the same idea.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a team leader at HONEYCOMB HOME CLEANING, a cleaning company with 22 employees that has doubled in size in a year. The founder (judge) wants your help keeping the team motivated as the company grows and changes.

The founder has added a new scheduling system, a second crew and a premium service. Employees say that they are confused about what the company is trying to become, and two crews are competing for the best routes. Turnover has risen to 30 percent, and customers have noticed that crew members seem less cheerful.

The founder (judge) asks you to explain how to communicate the company's vision, how to inspire the team, how to enlist employees to share that vision and how the company can adapt to its rapid growth.

You will present your recommendation to the founder (judge) in a role-play to take place at the company's office. The founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the team. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the founder's (judge's) questions, the founder (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What would you say in a team meeting to explain where the company is headed?
How could the founder settle the competition between the two crews?
scenarios.hook: A cleaning company doubled in a year and now 30 percent of its crew leaves annually.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an operations intern at ARTISAN CRATE CO., a company that sells gift boxes of locally made foods and crafts. The owner (judge) wants you to explain how the company's activities fit together as holiday orders triple.

ARTISAN CRATE CO. buys products from 26 local makers, packs the boxes by hand in a rented warehouse and ships them to customers across the country. Last year, a maker ran out of a best-selling jam two weeks before the holiday, and 180 boxes shipped incomplete. This year the owner expects 6,000 boxes, up from 2,000.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain the main types of business activities, how purchasing and production work together and how the supply chain can be managed to avoid shortages.

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the warehouse. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the holiday orders. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What could the company do if one maker cannot deliver on time?
How should the company decide how many of each product to order?
scenarios.hook: A gift-box company expects to triple its holiday orders after a jam shortage shorted 180 boxes last year.

scenarios.judge_role: branch manager of LAKEVIEW CREDIT UNION
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a member service representative at LAKEVIEW CREDIT UNION, a not-for-profit financial institution serving a small city. The branch manager (judge) wants you to explain money and payment choices to a group of high school students who will visit the branch next week.

LAKEVIEW CREDIT UNION offers checking and savings accounts, debit cards and small loans. Most of the visiting students have part-time jobs and are paid by direct deposit or by check, but many carry cash and have never used a savings account. The branch has 30 minutes with the group.

The branch manager (judge) wants to know what you will say about what money does, the different ways people pay for things, and why saving matters. You should also explain how a credit union differs from other places to keep money.

You will explain your ideas to the branch manager (judge) in a role-play to take place in the branch office. The branch manager (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the student visit. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the branch manager's (judge's) questions, the branch manager (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Why might a student choose a debit card over cash?
What is one reason a student should open a savings account now?
scenarios.hook: A credit union has 30 minutes to teach a room of teenagers how money works.

scenarios.judge_role: owner of SUNNY SIDE LAWN CARE
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an office assistant at SUNNY SIDE LAWN CARE, a landscaping company that hires about 15 seasonal workers each spring. The owner (judge) wants you to explain pay and deductions to a new group of employees, most of whom are receiving their first paycheck.

Several new workers were surprised that their first paycheck was about 15 percent smaller than the hourly rate multiplied by their hours. Two workers believed the company had made a mistake. The pay stub lists gross pay, federal and state taxes, Social Security and Medicare, and a small deduction for uniforms.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain how workers are paid, how to read a pay stub, why taxes are taken out, and how a new worker could plan a budget around take-home pay.

You will explain your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the company's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the paychecks. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What is the difference between gross pay and net pay?
How would you advise a worker to budget if their hours change each week?
scenarios.hook: Seasonal lawn workers open their first paychecks and find 15 percent missing.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a finance assistant at METRO MOTORS, a used-car dealership. The owner (judge) wants you to explain to a young first-time buyer how credit works before the buyer signs a loan.

The buyer, a 20-year-old with a steady job, wants a $12,000 car and plans to borrow the entire amount at 9 percent interest for five years. The monthly payment would be about $249, and the buyer would pay about $2,900 in interest. The buyer has one credit card with a $900 balance and has never taken out a loan.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain why credit matters, how to find the real cost of the loan, and how the buyer can use credit wisely and avoid taking on more debt than is manageable.

You will explain your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the dealership. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the loan. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What could the buyer do to lower the total interest paid?
What might happen if the buyer misses a payment?
scenarios.hook: A 20-year-old wants a $12,000 car loan and has never borrowed before.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an operations assistant at PIXEL PLAYGROUND, a small company that sells educational video games to schools. The founder (judge) wants to know why the company should keep careful financial records now that sales are growing.

PIXEL PLAYGROUND has kept its records in a folder of receipts and a checkbook. Sales rose from $60,000 to $140,000 in one year. When the founder applied for a small business loan, the bank asked for financial statements, and it took three weeks to put the numbers together. At tax time, the company could not find receipts for about $6,000 in expenses.

The founder (judge) asks you to explain what accounting does, why a business needs financial information and what records the company should keep.

You will explain your ideas to the founder (judge) in a role-play to take place at the company's office. The founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the records. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the founder's (judge's) questions, the founder (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Who else besides the founder needs to see the company's financial information?
How often should the company update its records?
scenarios.hook: A game company's sales more than doubled, but its receipts are still in a folder.

scenarios.judge_role: financial advisor of HARBOR WEALTH PARTNERS
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a client associate at HARBOR WEALTH PARTNERS, a small financial planning firm. The financial advisor (judge) wants you to explain the basics of planning to a 24-year-old client who has just received a $10,000 bonus.

The client has no debt other than a small student loan, saves very little and has never invested. A friend has urged the client to put the entire bonus into a single popular stock. The client also does not have renter's insurance or health coverage beyond what the employer provides.

The financial advisor (judge) asks you to explain how to set goals for the bonus, why starting early matters, the main types of investments and the role insurance plays in protecting the client's plans.

You will present your ideas to the financial advisor (judge) in a role-play to take place at the firm's office. The financial advisor (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the client. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the financial advisor's (judge's) questions, the financial advisor (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Why is putting all of the bonus into one stock risky?
What is one goal the client should set for the next year, and why?
scenarios.hook: A 24-year-old with a $10,000 bonus is urged to put it all into one stock.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a bookkeeper at BLOOM & BASKET, a florist with two employees and about $210,000 in yearly sales. The owner (judge) wants to know what to expect at tax time and what records to keep to avoid problems.

The owner has paid employees in cash for some weekend work, mixed business and personal charges on one credit card, and has not saved any money for taxes. The company received a letter from a state agency about unpaid sales tax from the previous year. The owner is worried about penalties.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain what taxes a small business and its owner may owe, which records must be kept and what legal responsibilities come with business and consumer financial products such as credit cards.

You will present your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the shop's back office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the tax letter. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What should the owner do first about the letter?
Why should business and personal spending be kept separate?
scenarios.hook: A florist gets a tax letter after mixing business and personal charges for a year.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a part-time cashier at CAMPUS CORNER CAFÉ, a coffee shop near a university. The owner (judge) wants you to give advice to a student employee who is deciding between working more hours and taking out a larger loan.

The employee earns $14 an hour working 12 hours a week and has $9,000 in savings. Tuition is $11,500 a year and the employee has been offered a $6,000 student loan. The owner also offers a retirement account match to employees who contribute at least 3 percent of pay, but the employee believes it is too early to think about retirement.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain the options for paying for college, why saving and investing matter even for someone this young and how the employee can make a responsible decision.

You will present your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the café. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the employee's choices. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What are the advantages of working more hours instead of borrowing more?
Why might the retirement match be worth using?
scenarios.hook: A student barista weighs a $6,000 loan against more shifts and a retirement match.

scenarios.judge_role: chief financial officer of NORTHBRIDGE FREIGHT
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a financial analyst at NORTHBRIDGE FREIGHT, a trucking company with 60 trucks and $18 million in annual revenue. The chief financial officer (judge) wants your advice on whether to replace 10 aging trucks this year or spread the purchases over three years.

New trucks cost $160,000 each and would reduce fuel and repair costs by about $22,000 per truck each year. The company could borrow at 7 percent. Fuel prices have been unstable, two large customers have not committed to contracts beyond next year, and cash on hand covers about six weeks of expenses.

The chief financial officer (judge) asks you to explain what role finance plays in a decision like this, what financial information is needed, how the time value of money affects the choice and what risks the company faces.

You will present your recommendation to the chief financial officer (judge) in a role-play to take place at the company's headquarters. The chief financial officer (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the trucks. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the chief financial officer's (judge's) questions, the chief financial officer (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How would losing one of the two large customers change your recommendation?
What information would you want before making a final decision?
scenarios.hook: A trucking company weighs $1.6 million in new trucks while two big customers hesitate to commit.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an office manager at BRIGHTSIDE DENTAL, a practice with three dentists and 12 employees. The owner (judge) wants to expand into a second office and needs help choosing where to get $350,000 in financing.

Three options are on the table: a large national bank offering a 6.8 percent rate with a lengthy approval, a local community bank offering 7.2 percent and a faster decision, and an equipment lender that would finance only the $120,000 of dental equipment at 8.5 percent. The practice currently owes $90,000 on its existing equipment and brings in about $1.4 million a year.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain the types of financial-services providers, what to consider in choosing one and how to avoid taking on more debt than the practice can handle.

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the owner's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the options. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Why might the lowest interest rate not be the best choice?
How could the practice tell whether it can afford the new debt?
scenarios.hook: A dental practice has three lenders, three rates and $350,000 on the line.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a business advisor at the TIDEWATER SMALL BUSINESS CENTER. The owner of TIDEWATER TEA CO. (judge), a small online tea retailer, has come to you after a data scare and wants help understanding the company's finances.

The owner lost a laptop containing customer payment information and financial files. No fraud has been reported, but the owner has not checked bank or credit accounts in months. The owner also has trouble separating the company's value from personal assets, owns the business outright, and has taken out a personal loan that is backed by the company's inventory.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain what accounting tells a business, how to tell what the owner and the business are each worth and how to protect the company and customers from identity theft.

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the small business center. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the lost laptop. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What steps should the owner take right away to protect customers?
Why is it useful to know the business's net worth separately from personal net worth?
scenarios.hook: A tea retailer's lost laptop holds customer payment data and months of unchecked accounts.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a front desk agent at SEASIDE INN, a 60-room hotel near a popular beach. The general manager (judge) wants you to explain why room rates change from season to season and from weekday to weekend.

SEASIDE INN charges $240 a night in July and $95 a night in February. Last month, a guest complained that the same room cost $60 more on a Saturday than on a Tuesday. A new 40-room hotel opened a mile away and lists its rooms at $15 below SEASIDE INN's rate.

The general manager (judge) wants you to explain how demand, competition and costs affect the prices a hotel sets, and how the inn can protect its profit throughout the year.

You will explain your ideas to the general manager (judge) in a role-play to take place in the manager's office. The general manager (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about room rates. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the general manager's (judge's) questions, the general manager (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What could the inn do in February to fill more rooms?
How should staff explain price differences to guests who ask?
scenarios.hook: The same beach hotel room costs $240 in July and $95 in February.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a server at DOCKSIDE GRILL, a seafood restaurant on a busy waterfront. The owner (judge) wants you to explain how to respond to a guest whose group was told that a reservation could not be honored.

The guest's party of eight arrived at 7:00 p.m. for a birthday dinner. The reservation had been entered for the wrong date, and the restaurant had no table for 45 minutes. The restaurant's policy is to offer a free appetizer when a reservation error is the restaurant's fault, but the manager is not working tonight. The guest is frustrated and has said so loudly.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain how you would handle the complaint, how you would explain the policy and how your words and tone can support the restaurant's service.

You will explain your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the restaurant's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the guest. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What would you say first to the guest?
What should you do if the guest asks for more than the policy allows?
scenarios.hook: A birthday party of eight arrives to find the restaurant booked their table on the wrong date.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a housekeeping supervisor at TRAILS END RESORT, a mountain resort with 90 rooms and a restaurant. The manager (judge) wants to know how to improve communication between housekeeping, the front desk and maintenance.

Guests have complained that rooms were not ready by the 3:00 p.m. check-in time, and that broken items reported at the front desk were not fixed. Housekeepers say they are not told when guests check out early, and maintenance says it often hears about problems by word of mouth days late. The resort has a short staff meeting only once a week.

The manager (judge) asks you to explain what effective staff communication looks like, which channels should be used for which kinds of messages and how the three teams can coordinate their work.

You will explain your ideas to the manager (judge) in a role-play to take place in the resort's office. The manager (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the guest complaints. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the manager's (judge's) questions, the manager (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What should be discussed in a short daily staff meeting?
How should an urgent repair request be passed along?
scenarios.hook: A mountain resort's guests wait for rooms because three teams never talk to each other.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a travel consultant at ISLAND TRAVEL CO., a small agency that plans vacations and group trips. The owner (judge) wants you to explain how to serve a group of visiting international clients well.

The agency will host 14 clients from three countries who are planning a two-week trip. Some speak limited English, others have dietary and religious needs that affect meals and schedules and one is traveling with an elderly parent. In the past, the agency lost a client who said staff were rushed and did not listen.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain what positive customer relations means in a travel business, how to build rapport and answer questions and how to show cultural sensitivity.

You will explain your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the agency. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the group. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How could you learn about each client's needs before they arrive?
What should you do if you make a mistake that offends a client?
scenarios.hook: A small travel agency prepares to host 14 clients from three countries after losing one for not listening.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an assistant manager at HARVEST TABLE, a farm-to-table restaurant with 35 employees. The owner (judge) wants your advice on safety, insurance and privacy after a kitchen accident and a guest-data concern in the same month.

A cook received a deep cut from a slicer and missed two weeks of work. The restaurant's insurance covered the medical costs, but the incident revealed that no written accident procedure existed. The same month, a server photographed a reservation book that listed guests' names and phone numbers and posted it online by mistake.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain what insurance does for a business, how a safe workplace is maintained, how accidents should be handled and why guest information must be kept private.

You will present your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the restaurant's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the incidents. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What should be included in a written accident procedure?
How should the restaurant respond to guests whose information was posted?
scenarios.hook: One restaurant's kitchen accident and a leaked reservation book arrived in the same month.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a human resources coordinator at CITY CENTER HOTEL, a 220-room downtown hotel known for its friendly service. The director (judge) wants to know how to protect the hotel's image as it hires 30 new employees for the summer season.

CITY CENTER HOTEL promises "a warm welcome in a busy city." In the past, new hires received only a one-hour tour and a handbook. Guest comments last summer said that seasonal workers seemed unsure of hotel services and sometimes gave conflicting information. The hotel's repeat guest rate fell from 38 to 31 percent.

The director (judge) asks you to explain what the brand promise means for employees, how an orientation could prepare new hires to support it and how everyday service can reinforce the hotel's image.

You will present your ideas to the director (judge) in a role-play to take place in the director's office. The director (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the seasonal staff. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the director's (judge's) questions, the director (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What should be covered on a new hire's first day?
How could the hotel check whether the new employees are living up to the promise?
scenarios.hook: A hotel's repeat-guest rate fell from 38 to 31 percent as seasonal hires gave guests conflicting answers.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a general manager at BAYSIDE BITES, a family-owned seafood restaurant that has operated in a small coastal town for 22 years. The owner (judge) has been asked to speak to a local civics class about the role a small business plays in the community.

BAYSIDE BITES employs 28 people, buys most of its fish from three local boats and sponsors the high school's baseball team. A town council member recently suggested that a large restaurant chain with national supply contracts would bring more jobs and tax revenue. Some residents agree, and others want to protect the businesses that already exist.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain how a private enterprise operates in a market economy, how small businesses affect an economy and what responsibilities a business has to the community it serves.

You will present your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the restaurant. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the civics class. After you have presented your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: How do small businesses and large chains each benefit a town?
What does it mean for a business to be private rather than owned by the government?
scenarios.hook: A 22-year-old family restaurant must explain to students what it gives a town that a chain might not.

scenarios.judge_role: chief executive officer of VOYAGE CRUISE & STAY
scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an operations analyst at VOYAGE CRUISE & STAY, a company that runs three small cruise ships and four coastal hotels. The chief executive officer (judge) wants your recommendation on how to respond to rising risks in the company's supply of food, fuel and staff.

Fuel costs rose 22 percent in a year. The company's seafood supplier has missed two deliveries, and a hotel in the company's most profitable location is short 14 employees going into the busy season. The company's insurance renews in 60 days, and the cost may increase by 18 percent.

The chief executive officer (judge) asks you to explain how the company's operations depend on a supply chain, what factors create business risk and which decisions you would make first.

You will present your recommendation to the chief executive officer (judge) in a role-play to take place in the executive conference room. The chief executive officer (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the risks. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the chief executive officer's (judge's) questions, the chief executive officer (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Which risk would you address first, and why?
How could the company reduce its dependence on one seafood supplier?
scenarios.hook: A cruise and hotel company faces 22 percent higher fuel costs, missed deliveries and 14 open positions.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a shift manager at THE COPPER KETTLE, a busy breakfast café with 20 employees. The owner (judge) wants your help resolving a conflict between the kitchen staff and the servers that has begun to affect guests.

Servers say the kitchen is slow and sometimes sends out wrong orders, and cooks say servers write unclear tickets and make changes after orders are sent. Last Saturday, a cook and a server argued within earshot of guests, and two tables left without ordering. Two of the café's best employees have said they may quit.

The owner (judge) asks you to explain how to communicate effectively with both groups, how to resolve the conflict and how to make sure both sides are treated with dignity and respect.

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place in the café's office. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the argument. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: What would you say to each group when you first meet with them?
How could the café prevent the same problem from returning?
scenarios.hook: A café lost two tables to a shouting match between cooks and servers.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an assistant director at EVERGREEN LODGE, a 120-room lodge that hosts weddings and corporate retreats. The director (judge) wants your advice on a decision that involves the lodge's honesty with a customer.

A couple's wedding weekend is in three weeks. The lodge discovered that its main ballroom's heating system failed inspection and that repairs may not be finished in time. Moving the wedding to the smaller ballroom would reduce capacity from 180 to 110 guests. The lodge could stay quiet and hope the repairs finish, but a cancellation would cost the lodge about $38,000 in contract revenue.

The director (judge) asks you to explain what ethical leadership looks like in this situation, how the staff should behave and how the lodge should respond to the dilemma.

You will present your recommendation to the director (judge) in a role-play to take place in the director's office. The director (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about the ballroom. After you have presented your recommendation and have answered the director's (judge's) questions, the director (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: When should the couple be told, and what should they hear?
How should the lodge treat the couple if the repair is not finished?
scenarios.hook: A lodge learns its wedding ballroom may fail inspection three weeks before a 180-guest event.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of a sales associate at PEDAL POINT, a bicycle shop in a mid-sized college town. The owner (judge) wants to know what marketing is and why the shop should spend time and money on it.

PEDAL POINT sells commuter bikes, mountain bikes and repair services. The owner has always believed that a good shop will sell itself, and has never planned any marketing. Last year a national chain opened a store 10 minutes away and began offering low prices on similar bikes. Since then, the shop's profit has dropped by 18 percent, and the owner is unsure what to change.

The owner (judge) does not understand what marketing includes beyond advertising. You must explain the main marketing functions and how they could help the shop compete and protect its profit.

You will explain your ideas to the owner (judge) in a role-play to take place at the shop. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking about marketing. After you have explained your ideas and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
followup_questions: Which marketing function should the shop work on first?
How can the shop compete without lowering all of its prices?
scenarios.hook: A bike shop's profit fell 18 percent after a national chain moved in.

scenarios.situation:
You are to assume the role of an assistant manager at SOLE SOCIETY, a store that sells athletic shoes and sports apparel. The store manager (judge) wants you to explain how to write an email to customers about a change to the store's return policy.

SOLE SOCIETY used to accept returns for any reason within 60 days. Because of a rise in worn shoes being returned, the store will now accept returns within 30 days, and only if the shoes are unworn. The store has 4,500 customers on its email list, ranging from high school athletes to parents shopping for children to older customers who walk for exercise.

The store manager (judge) is worried that a poorly written email will upset customers. You must explain how the email should be written, formatted and checked before it is sent, and how its tone should fit the different groups reading it.
